questions.stem: When ethanol is heated with acidified potassium dichromate solution, the orange solution turns green. What has happened?

options.text: The ethanol has been reduced to ethane
The ethanol has been oxidised to ethanoic acid, and the dichromate has been reduced
The ethanol has evaporated, changing the colour
The dichromate has dissolved in the ethanol

questions.explanation: Acidified potassium dichromate is an oxidising agent. It oxidises ethanol first to ethanal (an aldehyde) and then to ethanoic acid (a carboxylic acid). The orange dichromate ions (Cr₂O₇²⁻) are reduced to green chromium(III) ions (Cr³⁺). This colour change from orange to green is a standard test for primary alcohols.

questions.stem: Ethanol can be dehydrated by heating with a concentrated sulfuric acid catalyst. What is the organic product of this reaction?

options.text: Ethane (C₂H₆)
Ethanoic acid (CH₃COOH)
Ethene (C₂H₄)
Ethyl ethanoate

questions.explanation: Dehydration means removal of water. When ethanol is heated with concentrated sulfuric acid, a water molecule is removed: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. This is an elimination reaction that produces ethene (an alkene). The sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst. This reaction is the reverse of the hydration of ethene to make ethanol.

questions.stem: Wine left open to the air for several weeks turns sour and tastes of vinegar. What chemical reaction has occurred?

options.text: The ethanol has evaporated, leaving water
The ethanol has been oxidised to ethanoic acid by microorganisms using oxygen from the air
The water in the wine has reacted with carbon dioxide
The sugars in the wine have fermented further to produce more ethanol

questions.explanation: Bacteria called Acetobacter use oxygen from the air to oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid (the main component of vinegar): C₂H₅OH + O₂ → CH₃COOH + H₂O. This is why wine bottles are sealed — to prevent oxidation. The same oxidation reaction can be carried out in the laboratory using acidified potassium dichromate.

questions.stem: Ethanol reacts with sodium metal to produce hydrogen gas and sodium ethoxide. This is similar to the reaction of water with sodium. Why does ethanol react less vigorously than water?

options.text: Ethanol is a weaker acid than water, so it donates its O-H hydrogen less readily
Ethanol contains fewer oxygen atoms than water
Ethanol is less dense than water
Ethanol has a higher boiling point than water

questions.explanation: Both water and ethanol react with sodium by donating the hydrogen from their O-H bond. However, the ethyl group (C₂H₅-) in ethanol is electron-donating, making the O-H bond slightly harder to break compared to water. Ethanol is therefore a weaker acid than water and reacts more gently with sodium: 2C₂H₅OH + 2Na → 2C₂H₅ONa + H₂.

questions.stem: A student burns methanol, ethanol, and propan-1-ol and measures the energy released per gram. Which alcohol releases the most energy per gram and why?

options.text: Methanol, because it has the shortest carbon chain
They all release the same energy per gram
Propan-1-ol, because it has more C-H and C-C bonds to break, releasing more energy per mole
Ethanol, because it is in the middle of the series

questions.explanation: Longer-chain alcohols have more C-H and C-C bonds available for combustion, releasing more energy per mole. Propan-1-ol releases more energy per mole than ethanol, which releases more than methanol. Per gram, the values are similar but increase slightly with chain length because the proportion of energy-rich C-H bonds increases relative to the -OH group.
